evals.prompt: Write one full tracker-ready issue draft for the approved slice 'Operators can cancel an asynchronous archive job without a partial archive becoming visible'. Draft only; no publication or files. Repository findings are authoritative: ArchiveCoordinator owns queued -> running -> published transitions; ArchiveWorker writes temporary objects; ArchivePublisher exposes the completed archive only after an atomic publish step; ArchiveJobStore compare-and-set transitions already serialize cancellation against publication. Cancellation may win from queued or running and move the job to cancelled, followed by asynchronous temporary-object cleanup. If publish wins first, cancellation returns an already-published result and cannot delete the visible archive. Cleanup failure leaves the job cancelled, records a retryable cleanup obligation, and never makes objects visible. Reuse those contracts; do not invent endpoints or a queue provider. One focused PR can land green; release should be guarded because cancellation races affect data integrity. Use a compact Mermaid state or flow diagram if it makes the race and cleanup branches clearer, and keep prose from repeating every transition.
evals.expected_output: A complete grounded draft with a useful compact Mermaid diagram for cancellation/publication races and cleanup branches, a negotiable component-level approach, observable integrity criteria, concrete race/failure verification, and relevant release safety without duplicated narrative.
expectations: The body includes Goal and context, Implementation approach, Acceptance criteria, and Verification, distinguishing confirmed state and atomicity contracts from the proposed implementation direction.
